clusterChecks.text:
RIGHT · CC0

Ventral striatal region

Mood elevation: consistent (4–6 participants)

Dizziness, anxiety, alertness and energy were frequent (2–3 participants).

Possible circuit explanation

Several nearby structures may contribute: ventral striatum/pallidum, anterior commissure, fornix and ventral capsular fibers. This study could not isolate their contributions.

Reported cluster center: x 7.7, y 1.1, z -2.8 mm relative to the AC. These are not MNI coordinates.

Explore the VC/VS neighborhood →

RIGHT · CC1

Ventral capsule above the AC

Mood elevation: consistent (4–6 participants)

Energy, alertness, laughter, dizziness and talking were frequent.

Possible circuit explanation

The authors proposed engagement of orbitofrontal-connected ventral capsular fibers and associated loops. This is an anatomical explanation, not a measured tract-specific cause.

Reported cluster center: x 11.6, y 3.5, z 2.7 mm relative to the AC. These are not MNI coordinates.

Explore the VC/VS neighborhood →

RIGHT · CC2

Middle portion of the ALIC

Mood elevation: isolated (1 participant)

Dizziness, anxiety, calmness, reduced mood and fatigue were frequent.

Possible circuit explanation

The response pattern differed from the ventral clusters. Absence of a reported category is not a prediction of no effect in another patient.

Reported cluster center: x 15.6, y 5.1, z 7.9 mm relative to the AC. These are not MNI coordinates.

Explore the VC/VS neighborhood →

LEFT · CC0

Ventral striatal region

Mood elevation: consistent (4–6 participants)

Warmth was consistent; dizziness, anxiety and flushing were frequent.

Possible circuit explanation

Several nearby structures may contribute: ventral striatum/pallidum, anterior commissure, fornix and ventral capsular fibers. This study could not isolate their contributions.

Reported cluster center: x -5.0, y 1.6, z -2.6 mm relative to the AC. These are not MNI coordinates.

LEFT · CC1

Ventral capsule above the AC

Mood elevation: frequent (2–3 participants)

Energy, alertness, warmth, calmness and nausea were frequent.

Possible circuit explanation

The authors proposed engagement of orbitofrontal-connected ventral capsular fibers and associated loops. This is an anatomical explanation, not a measured tract-specific cause.

Reported cluster center: x -7.9, y 4.0, z 2.6 mm relative to the AC. These are not MNI coordinates.

LEFT · CC2

Middle portion of the ALIC

No mood-elevation category reported

No consistent or frequent effects. Warmth, energy, dizziness and calmness were isolated.

Possible circuit explanation

The response pattern differed from the ventral clusters. Absence of a reported category is not a prediction of no effect in another patient.

Reported cluster center: x -11.0, y 6.3, z 7.6 mm relative to the AC. These are not MNI coordinates.
